title: Digital logic and flip-flops
blurb: Read truth tables for logic gates, and explain how flip-flops and counters divide a frequency.

E7A01.why: **Bistable** means two stable states. A flip-flop holds either one until triggered. Gates have no memory.
E7A01.trap: AND and OR gates only follow their current inputs; they hold nothing.

E7A02.why: A decade counter counts to 10 and wraps: **1 output pulse per 10 input pulses**. Display decoding is a separate job.
E7A02.trap: Decoding a number for a seven-segment display is a decoder, not a counter.

E7A03.why: A flip-flop toggling on each clock pulse gives one output cycle per two input cycles: **÷2**.
E7A03.trap: XOR, OR and multiplexers combine inputs; none of them toggles and halves.

E7A04.trap: Don't divide 16 by 2 and stop; count the halvings, not the factor.

E7A05.why: An **astable** multivibrator has no stable state, so it switches back and forth on its own with no clock.
E7A05.trap: Flip-flops and T flip-flops need a clock to change; monostables need a trigger.

E7A06.why: A **monostable** has one stable state. A trigger moves it to the other state **for a set time**, then it returns.
E7A06.trap: A continuous square wave is an astable; storing a bit is a flip-flop.

E7A07.why: NAND is AND flipped: output is **0 only when all inputs are 1**, otherwise 1.
E7A07.trap: Output 1 only if all are 1 is AND; output 0 only if all are 0 is OR.

E7A08.why: An **OR** gate outputs 1 if **any** input is 1 (0 only when every input is 0).
E7A08.trap: Outputting 0 when all inputs are 1 describes NAND, not OR.

E7A09.why: XOR gives 1 when inputs differ. XNOR flips it: **0 if exactly one input is 1**, 1 if they match.
E7A09.trap: Outputting 1 when exactly one input is 1 is XOR, the non-inverted gate.

E7A10.why: A truth table lists **inputs and the resulting outputs for a digital device**.
E7A10.trap: Op-amps are analog; truth tables belong to digital logic.

E7A11.why: In positive logic **high voltage is 1 and low voltage is 0**.
E7A11.trap: It's about which voltage means 1, not noise immunity or a 'true' state.
